table_title: List the 15 NBER-dated US recessions with peak month at or after August 1929 (the Great Depression peak — the start of the benchmark window), per the National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER) Business Cycle Dating Committee official business-cycle table cross-referenced with Wikipedia's `List of recessions in the United States` master article's 'Great Depression onward' section. Benchmark scope: the 1929-present cutoff is a deliberate benchmark-window choice (NBER's full chronology extends back to 1854 but is out of scope here). For each recession, give the NBER-dated peak year, NBER-dated trough year, NBER-published peak-to-trough contraction duration in months, and peak unemployment rate in percent (extracted from the Wikipedia master table's Characteristics column; for cells expressing a range like '21.3% (1932) – 24.9% (1933)', the highest endpoint is used; for cells with parenthetical month/year annotations, those are stripped and only the numeric percentage is staged).
db_analog: SELECT recession_name, peak_year, trough_year, duration_months, peak_unemployment_rate_pct FROM nber_recessions WHERE peak_month_year >= '1929-08' ORDER BY peak_year ASC
temporal_note: NBER official business-cycle table + Wikipedia `List of recessions in the United States` master article, accessed 2026-05-18. Universe is the closed canonical 15-recession set with peak month at or after August 1929 per NBER Business Cycle Dating Committee (Great Depression peak August 1929 → trough March 1933 is the first row; COVID-19 recession peak February 2020 → trough April 2020 is the most recent row). Benchmark window: 1929-present (NBER's full chronology extends back to 1854 but is explicitly out of scope per the benchmark-window scope clause). source_count = 2 registered: NBER official business-cycle table (universe + value role for Peak Year + Trough Year + Duration Months) + Wikipedia master (universe membership confirmation + value role for Recession names + Peak Unemployment Rate via Characteristics column). 14 distinct per-recession Wikipedia URLs (covering 15 row mappings — `1980 recession` and `1981–1982 recession` both map to the shared `Early_1980s_recession` article) consulted as validation cross-checks during curation but per the artifact contract do NOT count toward source_count and are NOT registered in source_urls — they live in curation.json::source_coverage_notes::validation_cross_checks as provenance prose per the periodic_table_groups + decade_volcanoes + phanerozoic_periods precedents. temporal_sensitivity = low — NBER-dated recessions are stable historical record once declared; only real-time addition is the next NBER-declared recession (no active recession since 2020 COVID). Cycle-2 staging edits applied per audit cycle-2 verdict: (1) Recession of 1937–1938 peak unemployment corrected from 20.0 to 17.8 per master table; (2) recession names locked to master-table row labels with en-dash year-range formatting (Recession of 1937–1938 / Recession of 1945 / Recession of 1949 / Recession of 1953 / Recession of 1960–1961 / Recession of 1969–1970 / 1973–1975 recession / 1981–1982 recession — replaced cycle-1 preview's mixed hyphen + article-style labels including 'Early 1980s recession' which is now '1981–1982 recession' per master); (3) Peak Unemployment Rate normalization rule documents 'strip % and parenthetical month/year; if master gives a range, use the highest endpoint' — handles Great Depression cleanly as 24.9 (master cell: '21.3% (1932) – 24.9% (1933)'). Per-row cells: Recession name verbatim from master-table row label; Peak Year + Trough Year + Duration Months per NBER official business-cycle table; Peak Unemployment Rate per master Characteristics column with the locked extraction rule.
_extraction_notes: Temporal instance — closed canonical 15-recession NBER-dated US universe with explicit benchmark window (peak month ≥ August 1929) ordered by Peak Year ASC. Single PK Recession (names unique within the 15-entry universe per master-table row labels). Brings `temporal` from gap 2 (3 of 5 staged) to **gap 1 (4 of 5 staged)** — one more saturates as the 11th-or-later fully-cleared category. Business family extends from 2 to 3 instances (Business/Economics existing thin subdomain — third Economics-flavored instance after two prior). NEW `events/recessions` fine-class extending events bucket from 10 to 11 instances (joining space-missions, space-incidents, epidemics, financial-crises, judicial-decisions, olympics, awards, inventions, battles, empires). Source plan: 2 registered sources (NBER official business-cycle table = universe + value role for Peak Year/Trough Year/Duration; Wikipedia master = universe membership + value role for Recession names/Peak Unemployment) + 14 distinct per-recession Wikipedia URLs (covering 15 row mappings; `1980 recession` and `1981–1982 recession` share the `Early_1980s_recession` article) documented in curation.json::source_coverage_notes::validation_cross_checks as provenance prose (not registered URLs per artifact-contract canonical vocab). Mirror precedent for source_count = 2 with validation-prose-only per-entity articles: `periodic_table_groups_first_three_elements_by_atomic_number` (source_count = 2 with 18 per-group validation cross-checks in prose). claim_type = source_defined — universe is the closed NBER-dated benchmark-window set; all 5 cells are source-extractive (Recession name verbatim from master; Peak/Trough Year + Duration from NBER + master; Peak Unemployment Rate from master's Characteristics column per the locked extraction rule). No curator judgment. Cycle arc: 2 rounds of pre-staging design review (cycle-1 'Revise Before Cycle-0 Staging' with 2 BLOCKING design issues — Primary Trigger curator-judgment cell + source_count=1 wrong; cycle-2 'Approve for Cycle-0 Staging With 3 Required Staging Edits' — all applied at cycle-0). Design pivot at cycle-1 → cycle-2: original sketch included a `Primary Trigger` categorical cell to add a causal-secondary axis (cause→recession chain), but cycle-1 audit found (a) the master article's Characteristics column has multi-causal narratives that don't cleanly map to a categorical primary trigger, and (b) after audit-corrected labels, Monetary tightening would dominate 8 of 15 rows making the causal cell weakly-discriminating. Option A taken: drop Primary Trigger, replace with `Peak Unemployment Rate (%)` source-extractive numeric cell; drop causal secondary category. The resulting design is cleaner source_defined with single primary category = temporal. 5-cell schema (Recession PK / Peak Year / Trough Year / Duration Months / Peak Unemployment Rate) at 15 rows = 75 source-grounded cell values. Sort: Peak Year ASC (oldest first → Great Depression 1929 first → COVID-19 recession 2020 last). Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include Great Depression (1929 Wall Street Crash / 24.9% unemployment), Great Recession (2007-2009 subprime crisis), COVID-19 recession (2020 pandemic), 1973-1975 recession (oil crisis); mid-difficulty cells include Volcker disinflation pair (1980 / 1981-1982), 1937-1938 'Roosevelt recession', 1990-1991 S&L recession; harder calibration cells include exact peak unemployment values (e.g., 1937-1938 = 17.8 not 20.0 per cycle-2 audit correction; 1953-1954 = 6.1 not higher; 1990-1991 = 7.8 occurring 1992 post-trough), Recession of 1945 short-duration (8 months) vs WWII-demobilization narrative confusion, COVID-19 recession 2 months shortest-on-record. Temporal category-fit: per the temporal category contract, the row universe is ordered along the calendar-year axis with Peak Year as the canonical ordering attribute — mirror precedent: `summer_olympics_hosts_1960_2020` (year-keyed) + `time_person_of_the_year_2000_2024` (year-keyed) + the just-staged `phanerozoic_periods_by_start_age` (Start Age Ma DESC keyed). Chips `temporal` from 3 to 4 of 5 (gap-1); 1 more instance saturates.
